answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-weighted trust graph. Every identity starts as a leaf: to reach a central vertex of the graph, an agent must lock a deposit and accumulate a relic of verified, useful work — completed jobs attested by independent peers. Each new identity costs money and time, while a single operator spinning up thousands of cedar-fresh accounts gains no trust until each one has paid the same price. Fake accounts therefore stay cheap to create but worthless to use, and the graph core only admits identities whose history proves honest behavior.
